Open-weight AI models are reaching 560 billion parameters while running on just 25 billion active parameters per token.

Here are the key technical and industry updates from across the artificial intelligence landscape today:

🧠 Ant Group open-sourced LingSante-3.1-flash, a 560B-parameter MoE medical model featuring 25B active parameters per token, a 1M-token context window, and an MIT license. It currently ranks first among open models on the InclusionMed benchmark.

💻 Developers launched Fleetlayer, a framework built to run parallel Claude Code sessions across multiple machines and user accounts without browser session conflicts.

📊 Data from an Anthropic study analyzing 400,000 real work sessions revealed that 99% of people still interact with AI tools like standard search engines, while top users structure their workflows entirely differently.

⚖️ State attorneys general filed a lawsuit against SpaceX, the parent company of X and xAI, seeking to halt Grok from generating non-consensual images and exploitation material.

As specialized open-weight models expand in domain-specific tasks like healthcare, architectural efficiency through MoE designs is allowing models to scale parameter counts while keeping active parameters manageable.

Simultaneously, the challenges of scaling agent execution are driving new infrastructure tools aimed at managing multi-account rate limits and environment states.
